claim: PARIPRASHNA_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE_v0_1.md admits absence of cost/latency telemetry: §14A.2 states cost attribution per (user, channel, model) 'does not exist'; §17.8 states grep for ttft|first_token|histogram returns zero matches and per-request trace rows exist but are 'debugging, not aggregate'; §17.4 sets latency-budget targets (POST→turn.open <300ms, POST→first activity.upsert <1s, turn.close→interactive <100ms) with no stated measurement mechanism. Note: assumption A29 itself (§1.1, §6.6) is 'The instrument can ask' (clarification as a third planner outcome) and is textually unrelated to cost/latency — the dispatch's tie of this charge to 'A29' appears to be a labeling mismatch; the architecture claims actually under test here are the §14A.2/§17.4/§17.8 cost-and-latency-observability assertions (closer to A34 'cost governance', which is outside the A1-A32 range this shard's schema validates against).
reality: DB audit against the live Postgres instance confirms and sharpens the doc's own admission. `pg_tables` scan for cost/usage/trace/latency-named tables found four: query_trace_steps (493 rows, 2026-07-01→2026-07-18), llm_usage_events (0 rows), llm_provider_cost_reports (0 rows), llm_cost_reconciliation (0 rows). The three cost/token-accounting tables (llm_usage_events has input_tokens, output_tokens, computed_cost_usd, latency_ms, model, pipeline_stage columns — exactly the schema §14A.2/§17.8 says is missing) exist as schema but are 100% empty — dead/unwired infrastructure, never written to. The one populated table, query_trace_steps, has a latency_ms integer column but 0 of 493 rows have it populated (all NULL) — so even the 'per-request trace rows exist' claim in §17.8 overstates what's usable: latency is not actually captured. step_type is 'sql' for all 493 rows (no planner/retrieval/synthesis phase tagging) — so per-phase latency or cost breakdown is not computable even in principle from what's logged today. Cost-per-turn-by-model, cost-by-phase, planner latency distribution, tool-fetch latency distribution, and total time-to-answer p50/p95 (via percentile_cont) are all impossible to compute from live data: either the table is empty (cost) or the relevant column is entirely NULL (latency).

Verified absent on chat, with no place to put it... Cost attribution per (user, channel, model) so the observatory can see who is spending what — the panels exist; the attribution does not.

per-request trace rows exist (lib/trace/writer.ts:27,55,171-174) but grep for ttft|first_token|histogram across src returns zero matches. You cannot answer "what is p95 TTFT this week" without writing new SQL.

recommended_action: Treat §14A.2/§17.4/§17.8 cost-and-latency budgets as design targets, not measured baselines, until: (1) llm_usage_events is actually wired into the request path (it is schema-only today); (2) query_trace_steps.latency_ms is populated on every step (currently always NULL) and step_type/step_name is extended to tag planner/retrieval/synthesis phase, not just 'sql'; (3) a percentile_cont-based p50/p95 rollup is built once (1)-(2) are live. Until then, any 'cost per turn' or 'p95 latency' figure quoted elsewhere in planning docs is a guess, not a measurement. Also: correct the A29 cross-reference in the dispatching brief — A29 is the clarification-as-planner-outcome assumption, not a cost/latency assumption; the load-bearing assumption for this charge is closer to A34 (§14A, 'cost governance... blocking spend caps').

claim: No specific claim in the architecture doc addresses this — it is a new observation surfaced by direct DB inspection, not a check of an existing textual assumption.
reality: Three tables (llm_usage_events, llm_provider_cost_reports, llm_cost_reconciliation) exist in the production schema with a well-designed, cost-attribution-ready column set (provider, model, pipeline_stage, input/output/cache/reasoning tokens, computed_cost_usd, pricing_version_id, latency_ms, status) — this is exactly the shape §14A.2 says is needed and 'does not exist'. But all three are empty (0 rows each). This is dead schema: either a prior build-out that was never wired into the request path, or scaffolding for a future job that was never turned on. Worth flagging separately from PG1-D2-0001 because it changes the recommended remediation: the work is not 'design a schema for cost tracking' (already done) but 'wire the existing llm_usage_events insert into every LLM call path and stand up the reconciliation job that populates llm_provider_cost_reports/llm_cost_reconciliation' — a smaller, more scoped task than the architecture doc implies.
